en: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him.
when: Recite 100 times in the morning and 100 times in the evening. The Prophet ﷺ taught that the one who does so will not be surpassed on the Day of Resurrection except by someone who said the same or more.
src: Sahih Muslim; Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3469; Riyāḍ as-Ṣāliḥīn 1451.

ar: رَضِيتُ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيًّا
tl: Raḍītu billāhi Rabban, wa bil-Islāmi dīnan, wa bi-Muḥammadin nabiyyā.
en: I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, with Islam as my religion, and with Muhammad ﷺ as my Prophet.
when: A morning-and-evening remembrance renewing contentment with Allah, Islam, and the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
src: Sunan Ibn Mājah 3870 — graded Hasan in the cited edition.

ar: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
tl: Bismillāhilladhī lā yaḍurru maʿa ismihi shay’un fil-arḍi wa lā fis-samā’i, wa Huwas-Samīʿul-ʿAlīm.
en: In the name of Allah, with Whose Name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
when: Recite 3 times in the morning and 3 times in the evening as taught by the Prophet ﷺ, with a reported promise of protection from harm.
src: Sunan Ibn Mājah 3869 — Hasan; Riyāḍ as-Ṣāliḥīn 1457, citing Abū Dāwūd and at-Tirmidhī.

ar: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
tl: Aʿūdhu bi kalimātillāhit-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq.
en: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
when: Recite 3 times in the evening as an established evening remembrance seeking Allah’s protection.
src: Reported in Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī and other collections; Hisn al-Muslim 97 provides supporting references and grading notes.

ar: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا، وَبِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ نَحْيَا، وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُورُ
tl: Allāhumma bika aṣbaḥnā, wa bika amsaynā, wa bika naḥyā, wa bika namūtu, wa ilaykan-nushūr.
en: O Allah, by You we enter the morning, by You we enter the evening, by You we live, by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.
when: A Prophetic remembrance for entering morning and evening, acknowledging that our life, death, and return are under Allah’s authority.
src: At-Tirmidhī and Abū Dāwūd; Riyāḍ as-Ṣāliḥīn 1453; Hisn al-Muslim 78.

ar: اللَّهُمَّ مَا أَصْبَحَ بِي مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ أَوْ بِأَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِكَ، فَمِنْكَ وَحْدَكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، فَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ وَلَكَ الشُّكْرُ
tl: Allāhumma mā aṣbaḥa bī min niʿmatin aw bi-aḥadin min khalqika, fa-minka waḥdaka lā sharīka lak, fa-lakal-ḥamdu wa lakash-shukr.
en: O Allah, whatever blessing I or any of Your creation have received this morning is from You alone, without partner. To You belongs all praise and all thanks.
when: A morning remembrance acknowledging that every blessing comes from Allah; an evening form is also reported.
src: Abū Dāwūd, an-Nasāʾī and others; Hisn al-Muslim 81 notes a Hasan chain in its cited verification.

ar: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
tl: Allāhumma anta Rabbī lā ilāha illā Anta, khalaqtanī wa anā ʿabduka, wa anā ʿalā ʿahdika wa waʿdika mastataʿtu. Aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣanaʿtu. Abū’u laka biniʿmatika ʿalayya, wa abū’u laka bidhanbī, faghfir lī, fa-innahu lā yaghfirudh-dhunūba illā Anta.
en: O Allah, You are my Lord. None has the right to be worshipped except You. You created me and I am Your servant. I remain faithful to Your covenant and promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your blessings upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.
when: The Prophet ﷺ described this as the foremost form of seeking forgiveness and taught a special virtue for the one who says it with certainty during the day or night.
